entities.definition: The study of the museum-held modified human canine from the Late Neolithic Jablanica site in Serbia, published as DOI 10.1002/oa.70151, reassessing a specimen previously labelled an animal-tooth bead. This is the named research project, not all Balkan archaeology or a newly excavated burial.
entities.name: Markovic and Maricic's Jablanica human-tooth pendant reassessment

entities.definition: The reassessment's human-canine identification, workmanship and likely use as an ornament, with approximate dating from comparative evidence. The specimen was a surface find lacking secure excavation context, so exact age and circumstances of its former owner remain uncertain.
entities.name: A misidentified Jablanica museum specimen is interpreted as a Neolithic human-tooth ornament

entities.definition: The international research published in Earth's Future as DOI 10.1029/2025EF006095 on compound severe water scarcity across global wheat-growing regions and commodity prices, publicized by Aarhus University in August 2026. entities.definition: The study's severe-water-scarcity indicator, historical wheat-price association and warming-scenario price estimates, including a roughly threefold comparison at three degrees with the inflation-adjusted 2010 price. entities.definition: The ongoing climate-driven change in viticulture's growing cycles, wine quality, weather exposure and suitable regions, with growers' directly connected adaptation of varieties and sites. entities.definition: The synthesis of earlier grape-development cycles, heat/frost and disaster damage, modeled changes in suitable growing regions and growers' variety/slope adaptations. entities.name: Warming changes wine harvests, growing-region suitability and adaptation needs

entities.definition: The Canadian government's C$7.5 billion aid package for firms and workers affected by the specified US-Canada August 2026 tariff escalation. This mitigation-policy strand is distinct from imposing countertariffs; the source's US-dollar conversion is not a second package.

entities.definition: Peak Energy's planned $71-million sodium-ion factory near Sacramento, California, with operation targeted for 2027. This particular manufacturing ramp is distinct from GS1.1 design and the RWE/Jupiter deployments.
entities.name: Peak Energy's Sacramento-area sodium-ion factory development

entities.definition: The announced domestic factory plan, capacity and 2027 operating target alongside current reliance on Chinese cells and processing despite abundant sodium feedstock. The manufacturing ramp does not certify supply-chain independence or completed production.
entities.name: California manufacturing ramp and continuing Chinese supply dependence

entities.definition: The July 2026 announcement of the $71-million Sacramento-area factory. The original does not supply an exact announcement day in its body.
entities.name: Peak announces its California sodium-ion factory in July 2026

entities.definition: The separately named Peak Energy and RWE Americas pilot storage project near Milwaukee in the MISO region. It is not the California manufacturing project or Jupiter's supply contract.
entities.name: Peak Energy-RWE Americas Milwaukee-area sodium-ion pilot

entities.definition: The announced collaboration for a Milwaukee-area sodium-ion pilot intended to demonstrate regional grid backup. The report establishes a planned pilot, not completed commissioning.
entities.name: Peak-RWE sodium-ion grid pilot planning

entities.definition: The specific Peak-Jupiter Power agreement for grid-storage battery supply through 2030, worth up to $500 million. Other customers and the manufacturer's factory are not this procurement programme.
entities.name: Peak Energy-Jupiter Power sodium-ion supply agreement

entities.definition: The agreement's intended up-to-4.75-GWh supply and initial 720-MWh allocation, including Texas, as evidence of commercialization. Ceiling quantities and contract value are not achieved deployments.
entities.name: Planned sodium-ion deliveries under the Jupiter Power agreement

entities.definition: The observed worldwide replacement and expansion of public outdoor lighting with LEDs, including the energy-efficiency rebound and environmental consequences of that aggregate technology transition. The original describes rapid international adoption, over half of US streetlights by 2019 and further rollout toward 2030. This global adoption process does not make independent city installations, artworks, lighting standards or national laws one local project Event.
entities.name: Global public-lighting transition to LEDs

entities.definition: The transition's paradoxical increase in light pollution through excessive, unshielded and blue-rich illumination, with human circadian and wildlife harm despite efficient lamps. Harms are the effects strand, not evidence of a named new medical study.
entities.name: Excess LED illumination and circadian/ecological harm

entities.definition: The mitigation strand advocating coordinated dimming, spectrum/timing control, shielding and ecological dark periods to use LED capabilities without needless light pollution. Technical possibilities are not a completed worldwide smart-lighting deployment.
entities.name: Controllable LEDs and coordinated responsible-lighting plans

entities.definition: Constellation's restart programme for Three Mile Island unit 1, renamed Crane Clean Energy Center, targeting 835 MWe and service in 2027. It includes interconnection and nuclear restart approvals. Unit 2's 1979 accident, Eddystone's separate generation operations and unrelated Constellation projects are not this restart Event.
entities.name: Crane Clean Energy Center Three Mile Island unit 1 restart

entities.definition: The FERC waiver allowing transfer of existing Eddystone capacity interconnection rights to Crane, avoiding multiyear transmission-upgrade constraints and enabling earlier delivery for the planned data-center supply. It is an interconnection strand, not a final NRC operating authorization.
entities.name: FERC interconnection-rights transfer avoids Crane restart delays

entities.definition: The NRC's draft finding that the unit 1 restart would not cause significant environmental impacts. It is the environmental-review strand, separate from FERC interconnection relief and not final comprehensive restart approval.
entities.name: NRC draft no-significant-environmental-impact finding for Crane restart

entities.definition: FERC's approval of the waiver transferring 760 MWe of capacity interconnection rights from Eddystone units 3 and 4 to Crane. The original supplies no exact approval instant here.
entities.name: FERC grants the Crane-Eddystone interconnection-transfer waiver

entities.definition: The NRC issuance of the restart's draft finding of no significant environmental impact. No exact issuance date or final licence is inferred.
entities.name: NRC issues a draft environmental finding for Crane restart
